title: Can adversarial inputs neutralize a deployed steering vector by self-cancellation?

original_idea.body: Build a CAA safety vector, then embed the negative-class contrast prompts into the user input and measure how much steering collapses; sweep over count and paraphrasing across concepts.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: self-cancellation attack shows steering is unsafe as a standalone control.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: CAA vector + embedded-prompt evasion sweep; training-free.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (steering collapse vs embedded prompts).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Red-team robustness on open models, weak lab incentive.

novelty.reasoning: Self-cancellation shown narrowly; generality may be open.
